chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Karram, from Ibn Abi Yafur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he used to say:
O Allah, fill my heart with love for You, and fear of You, and affirmation and faith in You, and awe of You, and longing for You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor.

O Allah, make meeting You beloved to me, and make for me in Your meeting the best of mercy and blessing, and join me with the righteous, and do not delay me with the evil, and join me with the righteous of those who have passed, and make me with the righteous of those who remain, and take me by the way of the righteous, and assist me upon myself with what You assist the righteous upon themselves, and do not return me to evil after You have rescued me from it.

O Lord of the worlds, I ask You for faith that has no end until meeting You, causing me to live and die upon it, and resurrect me upon it when You resurrect me, and free my heart from show-off and fame and doubt in Your religion. O Allah, give me victory in Your religion, and strength in Your worship, and understanding in Your creation, and two portions of Your mercy, and whiten my face with Your light, and make my desire to be what is with You, and cause me to die in Your way upon Your religion and the religion of Your Messenger.

O Allah, I seek refuge in You from laziness, old age, cowardice, stinginess, heedlessness, hardness of heart, weakness, and poverty. And I seek refuge in You, O Lord, from a self that is not satisfied, and from a heart that does not humble itself, and from a supplication that is not heard, and from a prayer that is not beneficial. And I seek refuge in You for myself, my family, and my offspring from the accursed Satan.

O Allah, no one can protect me from You, and I find no shelter besides You, so do not abandon me, and do not return me to destruction, nor return me to punishment. I ask You for steadfastness upon Your religion, and affirmation of Your Book, and following of Your Messenger. O Allah, remember me with Your mercy and do not remember me with my sin, and accept from me, and increase me from Your grace, for I am longing for You.

O Allah, make the reward of my speech and the reward of my sitting Your pleasure with me, and make my deeds and my supplication sincere for You, and make my reward Paradise by Your mercy, and gather for me all that I asked You for, and increase me from Your grace, for I am longing for You.

O Allah, the stars have set, and the eyes have slept, and You are the Living, the Eternal. Neither the dark night hides from You, nor the sky with its constellations, nor the earth with its beds, nor the deep sea, nor the darknesses one upon another. You send down mercy upon whom You will of Your creation. You know the treachery of the eyes and what the chests conceal.

I testify with what You testified to Yourself, and Your angels testified, and the people of knowledge, that there is no god except You, the Mighty, the Wise. And for one who did not testify with what You testified to Yourself, and Your angels testified, and the people of knowledge, so write my testimony in place of their testimony.
O Allah, You are Peace and from You is Peace. I ask You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor, to free my neck from the Fire.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for general needs narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This comprehensive supplication (Du'a) from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) serves as a holistic guide for spiritual refinement, integrating theological affirmations with practical ethical requests. It is particularly significant in Shia tradition for its emphasis on purifying the heart from hidden vices like *riya* (show-off) and *ghaflah* (heedlessness), while anchoring the believer in the concept of *Tawhid* through the declaration of witness. The structure reflects the Shia scholarly focus on aligning internal states with external actions to achieve ultimate liberation from Hellfire.
